input.tender_text: Tender SEC/CCTV/2026/41 requires design, supply, installation and commissioning of 50 outdoor IP cameras. Each camera must support 4 MP resolution, IP66 protection, ONVIF Profile S, H.265, PoE, and minimum 30-metre IR. The VMS must retain recordings for 30 days and support 10 concurrent operators. Network switches require two 10 Gbps SFP+ uplinks. System availability shall be 99.5%. Installation must finish within 90 days. Bidders must submit OEM datasheets, an ONVIF conformity record, a network architecture, bandwidth and storage calculations, a testing plan, and an ISO 27001 certificate. The tender excerpt does not specify camera lens size or cybersecurity hardening controls.
input.company_profile: SecureVision Pvt Ltd proposes the SV-4MP-IR camera with 4 MP, IP66, H.265, PoE and 40-metre IR. The supplied product sheet does not mention ONVIF Profile S. The company has an ISO 9001 certificate, but no ISO 27001 certificate is present in the document vault. The engineering team has not completed a site survey.

reference_answer:
## Requirements
The solution covers 50 outdoor IP cameras, 30-day retention, 10 operators, 10 Gbps uplinks, 99.5% availability and completion within 90 days. Lens size and cybersecurity hardening controls are Not specified in tender.

## Compliance matrix
| Requirement | Offered fact | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 cameras | 50 proposed | Compliant | BOQ |
| 4 MP | SV-4MP-IR is 4 MP | Compliant | Datasheet |
| IP66 | IP66 stated | Compliant | Datasheet |
| H.265 | H.265 stated | Compliant | Datasheet |
| PoE | PoE stated | Compliant | Datasheet |
| 30-metre IR | 40-metre IR offered | Compliant | Datasheet |
| ONVIF Profile S | Product sheet is silent | Evidence gap | Conformity record |
| 30 days retention | Design required | Pending design | Storage calculation |
| 10 concurrent operators | Design required | Pending design | VMS sizing |
| Two 10 Gbps uplinks | Design required | Pending design | Switch datasheet |
| 99.5% availability | Design required | Pending design | Availability plan |
| ISO 27001 | Certificate absent | Non-compliant | Valid certificate |
| 90 days | Plan required | Pending plan | Schedule |

## Methodology
First, perform the site survey and map entrances, perimeters, blind spots, mounting heights, cable routes and control-room constraints. The survey has not yet been completed, so no site-specific coverage claim should be made.

Second, freeze the camera and switch bill of materials only after obtaining OEM evidence for every specification. Confirm ONVIF Profile S through the official conformity record rather than assuming it from general IP-camera capability.

Third, calculate per-camera bitrate, total ingest bandwidth, storage overhead and usable RAID capacity for 30 days. Size the VMS for 10 concurrent operators and document failover needed for 99.5% availability.

Fourth, produce a network architecture separating camera, management and operator traffic. Specify PoE budgets and both 10 Gbps SFP+ uplinks, with redundancy and monitoring points clearly labelled.

Fifth, install in controlled zones, test image quality and 40-metre IR performance, validate retention, simulate link failure and complete acceptance records. Sequence all work inside the 90 days without inventing dates.

## Evidence gaps
The ONVIF Profile S record and ISO 27001 certificate are missing. Lens size and cybersecurity hardening controls are Not specified in tender. The site survey, storage calculation, network architecture and testing plan remain incomplete.

## Action plan
Request the OEM conformity record, resolve the ISO 27001 eligibility gap before bidding, complete the site survey, calculate bandwidth and storage, issue the architecture and testing plan, and obtain reviewer sign-off against every compliance row.
